functionDeclarations.description:
Add a new note or update an existing note with the given title. Use this to remember information provided by the user. You can control whether the note appears in your system prompt with the include_in_prompt parameter. Notes can have attachments (images, documents) associated with them by providing attachment UUIDs.

To create a skill instead of a regular note, include YAML frontmatter with `name` and `description` fields at the top of the content (between `---` delimiters). Skills appear in the Available Skills catalog instead of the regular notes section and are loaded on demand via `get_note`.

Returns: A string indicating the operation result. On success, returns 'Note [title] has been [created/updated] successfully.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to add/update note [title]. [error details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: add_or_update_note

title.description: The unique title of the note.

include_in_prompt.description: Whether to include this note in the system prompt context. Default is true. Set to false for notes that should be searchable but not always visible.

append.description: Whether to append the content to an existing note instead of replacing it. Default is false. When true, the content will be added to the end of the existing note with a newline separator.

attachment_ids.description: Optional list of attachment UUIDs to associate with this note. These attachments will be returned when retrieving the note.

visibility_labels.description: Optional list of visibility labels for access control. Notes are only visible to profiles with matching grants. If not specified, new notes get default labels from config. Use an empty list [] to make a note visible to all profiles.

functionDeclarations.description:
Retrieve a specific note by its title to check its content, prompt inclusion status, and attachments. Returns the note's title, content, whether it's included in the system prompt, and any associated attachments.

Returns: A JSON string containing a dict with the note information. If note exists, returns {'exists': true, 'title': [title], 'content': [full content], 'include_in_prompt': [boolean], 'attachment_count': [integer]}. If note not found, returns {'exists': false, 'title': [title], 'content': null, 'include_in_prompt': null, 'attachment_count': 0}. Attachments are returned as multimodal content that vision models can see.
functionDeclarations.name: get_note

title.description: The title of the note to retrieve.

functionDeclarations.description:
List all notes with their titles, prompt inclusion status, and attachment counts. Can optionally filter to show only notes that are included or excluded from the system prompt.

Returns: A JSON string containing a list of note summaries. Returns an array where each item is {'title': [title], 'include_in_prompt': [boolean], 'content_preview': [first 100 chars], 'attachment_count': [integer]}. If no notes exist or match the filter, returns an empty array '[]'.
functionDeclarations.name: list_notes

include_in_prompt.description: Optional filter. If true, shows only notes included in prompt. If false, shows only excluded notes. If not specified, shows all notes.

functionDeclarations.description:
Delete a note by its title. This permanently removes the note from the system. Use with caution as this action cannot be undone.

Returns: A JSON string containing a dict with the operation result. On success, returns {'success': true, 'message': 'Note [title] deleted successfully.'}. If note not found, returns {'success': false, 'message': 'Note [title] not found.'}.
functionDeclarations.name: delete_note

title.description: The title of the note to delete.

functionDeclarations.description:
Delegates a specific user request to another specialized assistant profile (service) that might have different tools or capabilities. Use this if the main assistant cannot handle a request directly or if a specialized profile is more appropriate for the task. The target profile's 'delegation_security_level' (blocked, confirm, unrestricted) can override the 'confirm_delegation' parameter.

Available service profiles:
{available_service_profiles_with_descriptions}

Returns: A string containing the delegated service's response or an error message. On successful delegation, returns the text response from the target service. If service returns no text, returns 'Service [id] processed the request but provided no textual response.'. If service registry unavailable, returns 'Error: Service registry is not available to delegate the task.'. If target service not found, returns 'Error: Target service profile [id] not found.'. If delegation blocked by security policy, returns 'Error: Delegation to service profile [id] is not allowed.'. If confirmation required but unavailable, returns 'Error: Confirmation required to delegate to [id], but no confirmation mechanism is available.'. If user cancels confirmation, returns 'OK. Delegation to service [id] cancelled by user.'. If confirmation times out, returns 'Error: Confirmation timed out for delegating to [id].'. On delegation error, returns 'Error: Failed to delegate task to service [id]. Details: [error]' or 'Error from [id] service: An error occurred during processing.'.
functionDeclarations.name: delegate_to_service

target_service_id.description: The unique ID of the target service profile to delegate the request to (e.g., 'browser_profile').

user_request.description: The specific request, question, or prompt to be processed by the target service.

confirm_delegation.description: Optional. If true, explicitly ask the user for confirmation before delegating the task. Defaults to false. This may be overridden if the target profile's security level is 'confirm' (always confirm) or 'blocked' (never delegate). If the 'delegate_to_service' tool itself is configured to require confirmation for the current profile, user confirmation will also be sought.

attachment_ids.description: Optional list of attachment UUIDs to include with the delegated request. These attachments must be accessible in the current conversation and will be passed to the target service for processing.

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a reminder to be sent at a specific time. Use this tool when users ask to be reminded of something. Supports automatic follow-up reminders if the user doesn't respond.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Reminder scheduled for [time].' or 'OK. Reminder scheduled for [time] (with follow-ups every [interval], up to [N] times).' if follow-up enabled. On parameter error, returns 'Error: Invalid reminder parameters. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule the reminder.'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_reminder

reminder_time.description: The exact date and time (ISO 8601 format, including timezone, e.g., '2025-05-10T14:30:00+02:00') when the reminder should be sent.

message.description: The reminder message to send (e.g., 'Take your medication', 'Call mom', 'Submit the report').

follow_up.description: If true, will automatically send follow-up reminders if the user doesn't respond. Use for important reminders or when user says 'don't let me forget'.

follow_up_interval.description: Time between follow-up reminders (e.g., '30 minutes', '1 hour'). Only used if follow_up is true.

max_follow_ups.description: Maximum number of follow-up reminders to send. Only used if follow_up is true.

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a future trigger for yourself (the assistant) to continue processing or check on a task at a specified time. Use this for continuing work or checking task status, NOT for reminders. For reminders, use schedule_reminder instead.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Callback scheduled for [time].'. On invalid time format or past time, returns 'Error: Invalid callback time provided. Ensure it's a future ISO 8601 datetime with timezone. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule the callback.'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_future_callback

callback_time.description: The exact date and time (ISO 8601 format, including timezone, e.g., '2025-05-10T14:30:00+02:00') when the callback should be triggered.

context.description: The specific instructions or information you need to remember for the callback (e.g., 'Check if the download finished', 'Continue analyzing the data').

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a recurring LLM callback that will trigger repeatedly based on a recurrence rule (RRULE string). Use this for tasks that need to happen on a regular schedule, like daily briefings, weekly check-ins, or periodic reminders. IMPORTANT: Each recurring task creates individual callback instances that can be managed using list_pending_callbacks, modify_pending_callback, and cancel_pending_callback tools. To stop a recurring task entirely, you must cancel all its pending instances.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Recurring callback [task_id] scheduled starting [time] with rule [rule].'. On invalid arguments (RRULE format, past time), returns 'Error: Invalid arguments provided. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule the recurring task.'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_recurring_task

initial_schedule_time.description: The exact date and time (ISO 8601 format with timezone, e.g., '2025-05-15T08:00:00+00:00') when the *first* instance of the callback should run.

recurrence_rule.description: An RRULE string defining the recurrence schedule according to RFC 5545 (e.g., 'FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1;BYHOUR=8;BYMINUTE=0' for 8:00 AM daily, 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO' for every Monday).

callback_context.description: The context or instructions for the LLM when the callback triggers (e.g., 'Send a morning briefing with today's calendar events and weather', 'Check if any important emails arrived').

max_retries.description: Optional. Maximum number of retries for each instance if it fails (default: 3).

description.description: Optional. A short, URL-safe description to help identify the task (e.g., 'daily_brief', 'weekly_summary').

functionDeclarations.description:
Lists all pending LLM callback tasks for the current conversation, including:
- One-time callbacks from schedule_future_callback
- Reminder callbacks from schedule_reminder
- Individual instances of recurring tasks from schedule_recurring_task
Returns task IDs, scheduled times, and context for each pending callback.

Returns: A formatted string listing pending callbacks. If callbacks exist, returns 'Pending LLM callbacks:' followed by entries with '- Task ID: [id]
  Scheduled At: [time]
  Context: [context preview]'. If no callbacks found, returns 'No pending LLM callbacks found for this conversation.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to list pending callbacks. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: list_pending_callbacks

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of pending callbacks to list (default: 5).

functionDeclarations.description:
Modifies the scheduled time or context of a specific pending LLM callback task. You must provide the task_id of the callback to modify.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'Callback task [task_id] modified successfully.'. If neither new_callback_time nor new_context provided, returns 'Error: You must provide either a new_callback_time or a new_context to modify.'. If task not found, returns 'Error: Callback task with ID [task_id] not found.'. If task not an LLM callback, returns 'Error: Task [task_id] is not an LLM callback task.'. If task not pending, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] is not pending (current status: [status]). It cannot be modified.'. If task belongs to different conversation, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] does not belong to this conversation. Modification denied.'. On invalid new time, returns 'Error: Invalid new_callback_time. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to modify callback task. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: modify_pending_callback

task_id.description: The unique ID of the LLM callback task to modify (obtained from list_pending_callbacks or when it was scheduled).

new_callback_time.description: Optional. The new exact date and time (ISO 8601 format, including timezone, e.g., '2025-06-01T10:00:00-07:00') for the callback. If omitted, the time is not changed.

new_context.description: Optional. The new context or instructions for the callback. If omitted, the context is not changed.

functionDeclarations.description:
Cancels a specific pending LLM callback task by its task_id. Use this to:
- Cancel one-time future callbacks
- Cancel scheduled reminders
- Cancel individual instances of recurring tasks
- Stop a recurring task by canceling all its pending instances (use list_pending_callbacks first to find them)
Note: This cancels only the specific task instance identified by task_id.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'Callback task [task_id] cancelled successfully.'. If task not found, returns 'Error: Callback task with ID [task_id] not found.'. If task not an LLM callback, returns 'Error: Task [task_id] is not an LLM callback task.'. If task not pending, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] is not pending (current status: [status]). It cannot be cancelled.'. If task belongs to different conversation, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] does not belong to this conversation. Cancellation denied.'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to cancel callback task. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: cancel_pending_callback

task_id.description: The unique ID of the LLM callback task to cancel (obtained from list_pending_callbacks or when it was scheduled).

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule any action (wake_llm or script) to execute at a specific time. This is the general-purpose scheduling tool that complements schedule_future_callback. Use this when you need to schedule script execution or want more control over LLM callbacks.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. [action_type] action scheduled for [schedule_time]'. If invalid action_type, returns 'Error: Invalid action_type. Must be one of: [valid types]'. If wake_llm missing context, returns 'Error: wake_llm action requires 'context' in action_config'. If script missing script_code, returns 'Error: script action requires 'script_code' in action_config'. If schedule_time in past, returns 'Error: Schedule time must be in the future'. On invalid time format, returns 'Error: Invalid schedule_time format: [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule action. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_action

schedule_time.description: When to execute the action (ISO 8601 format with timezone, e.g., '2025-05-10T14:30:00+02:00')

action_config.description: Configuration for the action. For wake_llm: {'context': 'message for LLM'}. For script: {'script_code': 'Python code', 'timeout': 600}

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a recurring action (wake_llm or script) using RRULE format. This tool allows scheduling scripts to run on a recurring basis, complementing schedule_recurring_task which only supports LLM callbacks.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Recurring [action_type] action scheduled starting [start_time]' or 'OK. Recurring [action_type] action ([task_name]) scheduled starting [start_time]' if task_name provided. If invalid action_type, returns 'Error: Invalid action_type. Must be one of: [valid types]'. If wake_llm missing context, returns 'Error: wake_llm action requires 'context' in action_config'. If script missing script_code, returns 'Error: script action requires 'script_code' in action_config'. If start_time in past, returns 'Error: Start time must be in the future'. On invalid time format, returns 'Error: Invalid start_time format: [details]'. On invalid RRULE, returns 'Error: Invalid recurrence rule: [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule recurring action. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_recurring_action

start_time.description: When to start the recurring schedule (ISO 8601 format with timezone)

action_config.description: Configuration for the action. For wake_llm: {'context': 'message for LLM'}. For script: {'script_code': 'Python code', 'timeout': 600}

task_name.description: Optional. A short, URL-safe description to help identify the recurring task (e.g., 'daily_weather_check', 'hourly_metrics')

functionDeclarations.description:
Search previously stored documents (emails, notes, files) using semantic and keyword matching. Returns titles and snippets of the most relevant documents.

Returns: A formatted string containing search results. On success, returns 'Found relevant documents:' followed by numbered results with Title, Source, Document ID, optional original file availability (📎), Metadata, and Snippet. When original files (PDFs, images) are available, they are indicated with 📎 symbol and file info. Use get_full_document_content to retrieve the actual file. If no results found, returns 'No relevant documents found matching the query and filters.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to execute document search. [error details]' or 'Error: Query text cannot be empty.' or 'Error: Failed to generate embedding for the query.'.
functionDeclarations.name: search_documents

query.description: The natural language query describing the information to search for.

source_types.description: Optional. Filter results to only include documents from specific sources. Common sources: 'email', 'note', 'google_drive', 'pdf', 'image'. Use ONLY if you are certain about the source type, otherwise omit this filter.

embedding_types.description: Optional. Filter results based on the type of content that was embedded. Common types: 'content_chunk', 'summary', 'title', 'ocr_text'. Use ONLY if necessary (e.g., searching only titles), otherwise omit this filter.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of results to return (default: 5).

functionDeclarations.description:
Retrieves the full content of a document in the best available format using its unique document ID (obtained from a previous search). Returns original file (PDF, image, etc.) when available, otherwise text content.

Returns: ToolResult with file attachment when original file is available, otherwise a string containing the text content. When original file exists, returns both the file as an attachment and extracted text for context. For PDFs and images, you can analyze the file directly using your multimodal capabilities. If only text content is available, returns the full text content (raw content if available, or reconstructed from chunks). If document exists but no content available, returns 'Error: Document [id] found, but no content is available.'. If document not found, returns 'Error: Document with ID [id] not found.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to retrieve content for document ID [id]. [error details]'. Files larger than 20MB will fallback to text-only for performance.
functionDeclarations.name: get_full_document_content

document_id.description: The unique identifier of the document whose full content is needed.

functionDeclarations.description:
Submits a document from a given URL for ingestion and indexing by the system. Use this tool if the user asks you to 'save' a web page. The document will be fetched from the URL, its content extracted, processed, and stored to be made searchable. Provide a unique source_id for tracking this ingestion request.

Returns: A string indicating the ingestion status. On success, returns 'URL submitted. Service response: [message]. Document ID: [id]. Task Enqueued: [status].'. If ingestion fails, returns 'Error submitting URL for ingestion: [message]. Details: [error details]'. If configuration missing, returns 'Error: Server configuration missing (document storage path).'. On unexpected error, returns 'Error: An unexpected error occurred while submitting the URL. [error details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: ingest_document_from_url

url_to_ingest.description: The fully qualified URL of the document to ingest.

title.description: Optional. The primary title to assign to this document. If omitted, the title will be extracted automatically during the indexing process from the web page content.

source_type.description: A category or type for this document source, e.g., 'llm_url_ingestion', 'user_link_submission'.

source_id.description: A unique identifier for this specific document within its source_type. This should be unique for each ingestion request to avoid conflicts. A UUID is a good choice if one is not readily available.

metadata_json.description: Optional. A JSON string representing a dictionary of additional key-value metadata to associate with the document (e.g., '{"category": "research", "tags": ["ai", "llm"]}').

functionDeclarations.name: get_user_documentation_content

filename.description: The exact filename of the documentation file to retrieve (e.g., 'USER_GUIDE.md'). Must end in .md or .txt.

functionDeclarations.description:
Query recent events from the event system. Returns raw event data in JSON format for examining event structure and content.

Returns: A JSON string containing event data as a dict. On success, returns {'events': [array of event objects], 'count': [number], 'hours_queried': [hours], 'source_filter': [source_id or null]}. Each event object contains: event_id, source_id, timestamp (ISO format), event_data (parsed JSON), triggered_listeners (array of IDs). If no events found, returns {'events': [], 'message': 'No events found in the last [hours] hours'}. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to query recent events. [error details]' as a string.
functionDeclarations.name: query_recent_events

hours.description: Number of hours to look back (default: 1, max: 48)

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default: 10, max: 20)

functionDeclarations.description:
Test what events would match given listener conditions. Use this before creating a listener to ensure the match conditions are correct. Returns events that would have triggered the listener.

Returns: A JSON string containing test results as a dict. On success, returns {'matched_events': [array of matching events], 'total_tested': [number], 'matched_count': [number], 'match_conditions': [conditions used], 'hours_queried': [hours], 'analysis': [optional array of analysis messages]}. Each matched event contains: event_id, timestamp (ISO format), event_data. If no events to test, returns similar structure with 'message' explaining no events found. If match_conditions empty, returns {'error': 'match_conditions cannot be empty', 'message': 'Please provide at least one condition to test'}. When no events match and validation is available, analysis will include validation errors and suggestions. On other errors, returns {'error': 'Failed to test event listener: [error details]', 'match_conditions': [conditions used]}.
functionDeclarations.name: test_event_listener

match_conditions.description: Match conditions to test. Use dot notation for nested fields (e.g., {'entity_id': 'person.alex', 'new_state.state': 'Home'})

hours.description: Number of hours to look back (default: 24, max: 48)

limit.description: Maximum number of matching events to return (default: 10, max: 20)

functionDeclarations.description:
Create a new automation (event-triggered or schedule-based).

Event automations trigger when specific events occur (e.g., email received, calendar event).
Schedule automations run on a recurring schedule using RRULE format.

IMPORTANT: Times in RRULE strings (BYHOUR, BYMINUTE, etc.) are interpreted in the user's
configured timezone, NOT UTC. For example, if the user is in Australia/Sydney and asks for
"every day at 9am", use BYHOUR=9 — the system will schedule it at 9am Sydney time.

Examples:
- Event: "Send me a reminder when I receive an email from work"
- Schedule: "Wake me up every weekday at 7am" (RRULE: FREQ=DAILY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYHOUR=7;BYMINUTE=0)
functionDeclarations.name: create_automation

automation_type.description: Type of automation: 'event' for event-triggered, 'schedule' for time-based

trigger_config.description:
Configuration for the trigger.
For event automations:
  - event_source: string (e.g., 'email_received', 'calendar_event')
  - event_filter: object with filtering criteria

For schedule automations:
  - recurrence_rule: RRULE string (e.g., 'FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=7;BYMINUTE=0'). Times are in the user's configured timezone.

action_type.description: Action to perform: 'wake_llm' to notify you, 'script' to run code

action_config.description:
Configuration for the action.
For wake_llm:
  - context: string with optional context for the LLM

For script:
  - script_code: Python code to execute
  - task_name: optional name for the script execution

description.description: Optional description of what this automation does

functionDeclarations.description: List all automations, optionally filtered by type (event/schedule) or enabled status
functionDeclarations.name: list_automations

automation_type.description: Filter by automation type (omit to show all)

functionDeclarations.description: Get details of a specific automation by ID
functionDeclarations.name: get_automation

functionDeclarations.description: Update an existing automation's configuration
functionDeclarations.name: update_automation

automation_id.description: ID of the automation to update

functionDeclarations.description: Enable a disabled automation
functionDeclarations.name: enable_automation

functionDeclarations.description: Disable an automation temporarily (can be re-enabled later)
functionDeclarations.name: disable_automation

functionDeclarations.description: Permanently delete an automation
functionDeclarations.name: delete_automation

functionDeclarations.description: Get execution statistics and recent history for an automation
functionDeclarations.name: get_automation_stats
download_state_history

entity_ids.description: Optional list of entity IDs to retrieve history for (e.g., ['sensor.temperature', 'light.living_room']). If not provided, retrieves history for all entities. Be cautious with all entities as it may return a large dataset.

start_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp for the start of the history period (e.g., '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'). If not provided, defaults to 24 hours ago.

end_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp for the end of the history period (e.g., '2024-01-02T00:00:00Z'). If not provided, defaults to current time.

significant_changes_only.description: If true, only return significant state changes (filters out minor updates). Defaults to false.

functionDeclarations.description:
Renders a Home Assistant Jinja2 template and returns the result. This tool allows you to evaluate templates using Home Assistant's current state, including all entities, attributes, and template functions available in HA. Common uses include getting entity states, performing calculations, or formatting data using Home Assistant's template engine.

Returns: A string containing the rendered template result. On success, returns the evaluated template output as a string (empty results return 'Template rendered to empty result'). If HA not configured, returns 'Error: Home Assistant integration is not configured or available.'. If HA API not installed, returns 'Error: Home Assistant API library is not installed.'. On API error, returns 'Error: Home Assistant API error - [error details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to render template - [error details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: render_home_assistant_template

template.description: The Jinja2 template string to render. Can use all Home Assistant template functions and filters, such as states(), state_attr(), now(), as_timestamp(), etc. Example: '{{ states("sensor.temperature") }}'

functionDeclarations.description:
Retrieves a current snapshot/image from a Home Assistant camera entity. The image will be displayed to you for analysis. If no camera_entity_id is provided, returns a list of available cameras.

Common camera entities include doorbell cameras, security cameras, and webcams. Examples: camera.front_door, camera.doorbell_camera, camera.backyard_cam

Returns: Captures and displays the camera image to the user when entity_id is provided. Without entity_id, returns list of available cameras. On errors, returns descriptive error messages.
functionDeclarations.name: get_camera_snapshot

camera_entity_id.description: The Home Assistant entity ID of the camera (e.g., 'camera.front_door'). If not provided, returns a list of all available camera entities.

functionDeclarations.description:
List and search Home Assistant entities by ID, name, or area. Returns entities with their IDs, friendly names, areas, and devices. Useful for discovering what sensors, lights, switches, cameras, and other entities are available in your Home Assistant setup.

The entity_id_filter parameter does substring matching, so you can search by:
- Entity type: 'sensor', 'light', 'switch', 'binary_sensor'
- Function: 'temperature', 'motion', 'energy', 'camera'
- Specific entity: 'pool', 'living_room', 'garage'
- Combined: 'sensor.pool' finds pool sensors, 'light.living' finds living room lights

Examples:
- list_home_assistant_entities(entity_id_filter='temperature') → all temperature sensors
- list_home_assistant_entities(entity_id_filter='light.living') → living room lights
- list_home_assistant_entities(area_filter='pool') → all pool equipment
- list_home_assistant_entities(entity_id_filter='motion') → motion sensors

Results are cached for 2 minutes to improve performance.
functionDeclarations.name: list_home_assistant_entities

entity_id_filter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to filter entity IDs. Since entity IDs follow the pattern 'domain.name' (e.g., 'sensor.pool_temperature'), you can filter by domain ('sensor'), function ('temperature'), location ('pool'), or combinations ('sensor.pool'). Matches any part of the entity ID.

area_filter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to filter by area name (e.g., 'living room', 'pool', 'garage', 'bedroom'). Only returns entities assigned to areas matching this substring.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 50. Maximum allowed is 200. Use filters to narrow results if needed.

functionDeclarations.description: List all configured security cameras with their status. Returns camera IDs, names, status (online/offline), and backend type. Use this first to discover available cameras before querying events or frames.
functionDeclarations.name: list_cameras

functionDeclarations.description:
Search for AI detection events (person, vehicle, pet, motion) on a camera within a time range. Returns events with timestamps, types, and confidence levels.

This is typically the FIRST STEP in investigating 'what happened' questions. Use the results to identify time periods of interest, then use get_camera_frames_batch or get_camera_frame to visually examine those periods.

Example: To find when chickens escaped, search for 'pet' events on the coop camera.
functionDeclarations.name: search_camera_events

start_time.description: Start of time range in LOCAL TIME (e.g., '2024-01-15T08:00:00' or '2024-01-15T08:00'). Use local time, not UTC.

end_time.description: End of time range in LOCAL TIME (e.g., '2024-01-15T18:00:00'). Use local time, not UTC.

event_types.description: Optional filter for event types. Valid types: 'person', 'vehicle', 'pet', 'motion'. If not specified, returns all event types.

functionDeclarations.description:
Get a single frame/thumbnail from a camera at a specific timestamp. Returns a JPEG image attachment.

Use this to examine a SPECIFIC moment identified from events or batch frame analysis. The timestamp should be within a recorded period (use get_camera_recordings to check).
functionDeclarations.name: get_camera_frame

timestamp.description: Exact timestamp in LOCAL TIME (e.g., '2024-01-15T14:30:00'). Use local time, not UTC.

functionDeclarations.description:

functionDeclarations.description:
Execute a Python script in a sandboxed environment for automation and complex operations.

**IMPORTANT: Before writing scripts, please read the scripting documentation first!**
Use the command: `get_user_documentation_content filename='scripting.md'`

**Tool Documentation:**
To see available tools and their parameters, ask: 'Show me the available tools'

**Execution Environment:**
• Timeout: 10 minutes maximum execution time (to allow for external API calls)
• Sandboxed: No file system or network access
• Deterministic: No random numbers or current time

**Sandbox Limitations:**
The Monty scripting engine runs a sandboxed Python subset with these restrictions:
• No class definitions (can't use `class` keyword)
• No generators or yield statements
• No match/case statements
• No context managers or with statements
• No del statement
• No dict unpacking in literals ({**d1, **d2} not supported)
• No str.format() method (use f-strings instead)
• No map/filter functions (use list comprehensions instead)
• Decorators are buggy (avoid using them)
• Exceptions only accept 0 or 1 string arguments
• No imports except heavily sandboxed os, sys, typing, pathlib modules
• Resource limits: 256MB memory, 100 recursion depth
• However: try/except, while loops, float(), set(), frozenset() ARE supported

**Built-in Functions:**
• Type conversions: bool(), int(), str(), list(), tuple(), dict()
• Collections: len(), range(), sorted(), reversed(), enumerate(), zip()
• Logic: all(), any(), max(), min()
• Object inspection: type(), dir(), getattr(), hasattr()
• Control: print(), fail()
• JSON: json_encode(value), json_decode(value)
• LLM Wake: wake_llm(context, include_event=True) - Request LLM attention with context (string or dict)

**Family Assistant Tools:**
All enabled tools are available as functions. Call them directly:
• add_or_update_note(title='...', content='...')
• search_notes(query='...')
• send_email(to='...', subject='...', body='...')

**Note**: Tools return structured data (dicts, lists) directly. You can use results
immediately without parsing. `json_decode()` is safe to call on any value - it passes
through dicts, lists, numbers, and booleans unchanged, and only parses strings:
```python
notes = search_notes(query='TODO')  # Returns a list directly
for note in notes:
    print(note['title'])
```

**Tools API Functions:**
• tools_list() - List all available tools with descriptions
• tools_get(name) - Get detailed info about a specific tool
• tools_execute(name, **kwargs) - Execute a tool by name

**Attachment API Functions:**
• attachment_get(attachment_id) - Get attachment metadata by ID
• attachment_create(content, filename, description, mime_type) - Create new attachment
Note: attachment_list() and attachment_send() are not available.
Scripts must receive attachment IDs from LLM context, tool results, or parameters.

**Returning Attachments:**
Attachments created by tools or attachment_create() are represented as dictionaries
with metadata: {"id": uuid, "filename": str, "mime_type": str, "size": int, "description": str}
Return these dicts to make attachments visible to the LLM:

```python
# Single attachment - last expression is returned
data = attachment_create(content="data", filename="data.txt", mime_type="text/plain")
data  # Dict with attachment info, automatically sent to LLM

# Multiple attachments - return list
chart1 = create_chart(data1)  # Returns dict
chart2 = create_chart(data2)  # Returns dict
[chart1, chart2]  # Both dicts visible to LLM

# Functional composition (recommended for data viz)
chart = create_vega_chart(
    spec=spec,
    data_attachments=[jq_query(source, '.[] | select(.value > 10)')]
)
chart  # Returns attachment dict
```

**Example Scripts:**

1. Simple note creation:
```python
result = add_or_update_note(
    title='Meeting Notes',
    content='Discussed project timeline'
)
print('Created note:', result)
```

2. Conditional logic with search:
```python
def process_todos():
    notes = search_notes(query='TODO')
    
    if len(notes) > 0:
        print('Found', len(notes), 'TODO items')
        for note in notes:
            print('-', note['title'])
    else:
        print('No TODO items found')
    return notes

# Call the function
process_todos()
```

3. Complex automation:
```python
def create_project_summary():
    # Search for notes, create summary, send email
    project_notes = search_notes(query='Project Alpha')
    
    summary = 'Project Alpha Summary:\n\n'
    for note in project_notes:
        summary += '- ' + note['title'] + '\n'
    
    if len(project_notes) > 0:
        add_or_update_note(
            title='Project Alpha Summary',
            content=summary
        )
        result = send_email(
            to='team@example.com',
            subject='Weekly Project Summary',
            body=summary
        )
        return {'notes_found': len(project_notes), 'email_result': result}
    else:
        return {'notes_found': 0, 'email_result': 'No notes to summarize'}

# Execute the function
create_project_summary()
```

4. Working with user attachments (attachment ID provided by LLM):
```python
# Attachment ID passed to script by LLM based on conversation context
# Example: LLM calls execute_script with attachment_id parameter
def process_user_attachment(attachment_id):
    # Get attachment details
    attachment_info = attachment_get(attachment_id)
    
    if attachment_info:
        print('Processing:', attachment_info['description'])
        
        # Process the attachment with a tool (ID auto-converted to content)
        if 'image' in attachment_info['mime_type']:
            analysis = tools_execute('analyze_image', image_data=attachment_id)
            # Send results back to user via LLM tools
            wake_llm({'message': 'Analysis: ' + analysis, 'attachments': [attachment_id]})
        else:
            # Use attach_to_response LLM tool to send attachment back
            tools_execute('attach_to_response', attachment_ids=[attachment_id])
    else:
        print('Attachment not found or not accessible')

# Call with attachment ID from LLM context
# process_user_attachment('uuid-from-llm-context')
```

5. Data visualization with automatic attachment propagation:
```python
# Create a chart - attachment automatically returns to LLM
spec = {
  '$schema': 'https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json',
  'data': {'name': 'sensor_data'},
  'mark': 'line',
  'encoding': {
    'x': {'field': 'timestamp', 'type': 'temporal'},
    'y': {'field': 'temperature', 'type': 'quantitative'}
  }
}

# Chart is automatically visible - no need for attach_to_response!
create_vega_chart(
  spec=json_encode(spec),
  data_attachments=[sensor_attachment_id],
  title='Temperature Over Time'
)
```

6. Multi-chart dashboard:
```python
# Create multiple related charts
temp_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'line', ...}
humidity_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'area', ...}

temp_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(temp_spec), data_attachments=[data])
humidity_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(humidity_spec), data_attachments=[data])

# Both charts automatically visible to LLM
[temp_chart, humidity_chart]
```

functionDeclarations.description:
Execute a Python script in a sandboxed environment for automation and complex operations.

**IMPORTANT: Before writing scripts, please read the scripting documentation first!**
Use the command: `get_user_documentation_content filename='scripting.md'`

**Tool Documentation:**
To see available tools and their parameters, ask: 'Show me the available tools'

**Execution Environment:**
• Timeout: 10 minutes maximum execution time (to allow for external API calls)
• Sandboxed: No file system or network access
• Deterministic: No random numbers or current time

**Sandbox Limitations:**
The Monty scripting engine runs a sandboxed Python subset with these restrictions:
• No class definitions (can't use `class` keyword)
• No generators or yield statements
• No match/case statements
• No context managers or with statements
• No del statement
• No dict unpacking in literals ({**d1, **d2} not supported)
• No str.format() method (use f-strings instead)
• No map/filter functions (use list comprehensions instead)
• Decorators are buggy (avoid using them)
• Exceptions only accept 0 or 1 string arguments
• No imports except heavily sandboxed os, sys, typing, pathlib modules
• Resource limits: 256MB memory, 100 recursion depth
• However: try/except, while loops, float(), set(), frozenset() ARE supported

**Built-in Functions:**
• Type conversions: bool(), int(), str(), list(), tuple(), dict()
• Collections: len(), range(), sorted(), reversed(), enumerate(), zip()
• Logic: all(), any(), max(), min()
• Object inspection: type(), dir(), getattr(), hasattr()
• Control: print(), fail()
• JSON: json_encode(value), json_decode(value)
• LLM Wake: wake_llm(context, include_event=True) - Request LLM attention with context (string or dict)

**Family Assistant Tools:**
All enabled tools are available as functions. Call them directly:
• add_or_update_note(title='...', content='...')
• search_notes(query='...')
• send_email(to='...', subject='...', body='...')

**Note**: Tools return structured data (dicts, lists) directly. You can use results
immediately without parsing. `json_decode()` is safe to call on any value - it passes
through dicts, lists, numbers, and booleans unchanged, and only parses strings:
```python
notes = search_notes(query='TODO')  # Returns a list directly
for note in notes:
    print(note['title'])
```

**Tools API Functions:**
• tools_list() - List all available tools with descriptions
• tools_get(name) - Get detailed info about a specific tool
• tools_execute(name, **kwargs) - Execute a tool by name

**Attachment API Functions:**
• attachment_get(attachment_id) - Get attachment metadata by ID
• attachment_create(content, filename, description, mime_type) - Create new attachment
Note: attachment_list() and attachment_send() are not available.
Scripts must receive attachment IDs from LLM context, tool results, or parameters.

**Returning Attachments:**
Attachments created by tools or attachment_create() are represented as dictionaries
with metadata: {"id": uuid, "filename": str, "mime_type": str, "size": int, "description": str}
Return these dicts to make attachments visible to the LLM:

```python
# Single attachment - last expression is returned
data = attachment_create(content="data", filename="data.txt", mime_type="text/plain")
data  # Dict with attachment info, automatically sent to LLM

# Multiple attachments - return list
chart1 = create_chart(data1)  # Returns dict
chart2 = create_chart(data2)  # Returns dict
[chart1, chart2]  # Both dicts visible to LLM

# Functional composition (recommended for data viz)
chart = create_vega_chart(
    spec=spec,
    data_attachments=[jq_query(source, '.[] | select(.value > 10)')]
)
chart  # Returns attachment dict
```

**Example Scripts:**

1. Simple note creation:
```python
result = add_or_update_note(
    title='Meeting Notes',
    content='Discussed project timeline'
)
print('Created note:', result)
```

2. Conditional logic with search:
```python
def process_todos():
    notes = search_notes(query='TODO')
    
    if len(notes) > 0:
        print('Found', len(notes), 'TODO items')
        for note in notes:
            print('-', note['title'])
    else:
        print('No TODO items found')
    return notes

# Call the function
process_todos()
```

3. Complex automation:
```python
def create_project_summary():
    # Search for notes, create summary, send email
    project_notes = search_notes(query='Project Alpha')
    
    summary = 'Project Alpha Summary:\n\n'
    for note in project_notes:
        summary += '- ' + note['title'] + '\n'
    
    if len(project_notes) > 0:
        add_or_update_note(
            title='Project Alpha Summary',
            content=summary
        )
        result = send_email(
            to='team@example.com',
            subject='Weekly Project Summary',
            body=summary
        )
        return {'notes_found': len(project_notes), 'email_result': result}
    else:
        return {'notes_found': 0, 'email_result': 'No notes to summarize'}

# Execute the function
create_project_summary()
```

4. Working with user attachments (attachment ID provided by LLM):
```python
# Attachment ID passed to script by LLM based on conversation context
# Example: LLM calls execute_script with attachment_id parameter
def process_user_attachment(attachment_id):
    # Get attachment details
    attachment_info = attachment_get(attachment_id)
    
    if attachment_info:
        print('Processing:', attachment_info['description'])
        
        # Process the attachment with a tool (ID auto-converted to content)
        if 'image' in attachment_info['mime_type']:
            analysis = tools_execute('analyze_image', image_data=attachment_id)
            # Send results back to user via LLM tools
            wake_llm({'message': 'Analysis: ' + analysis, 'attachments': [attachment_id]})
        else:
            # Use attach_to_response LLM tool to send attachment back
            tools_execute('attach_to_response', attachment_ids=[attachment_id])
    else:
        print('Attachment not found or not accessible')

# Call with attachment ID from LLM context
# process_user_attachment('uuid-from-llm-context')
```

5. Data visualization with automatic attachment propagation:
```python
# Create a chart - attachment automatically returns to LLM
spec = {
  '$schema': 'https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json',
  'data': {'name': 'sensor_data'},
  'mark': 'line',
  'encoding': {
    'x': {'field': 'timestamp', 'type': 'temporal'},
    'y': {'field': 'temperature', 'type': 'quantitative'}
  }
}

# Chart is automatically visible - no need for attach_to_response!
create_vega_chart(
  spec=json_encode(spec),
  data_attachments=[sensor_attachment_id],
  title='Temperature Over Time'
)
```

6. Multi-chart dashboard:
```python
# Create multiple related charts
temp_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'line', ...}
humidity_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'area', ...}

temp_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(temp_spec), data_attachments=[data])
humidity_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(humidity_spec), data_attachments=[data])

# Both charts automatically visible to LLM
[temp_chart, humidity_chart]
```
functionDeclarations.name: execute_script

script.description:
The Python script code to execute. Must be valid Python syntax.

The script can:
• Define variables and functions
• Use control flow (if/else, for loops)
• Call any available Family Assistant tool
• Process and transform data
• Print output for debugging
• Return a value (the last expression is returned)

Scripts should be self-contained and handle errors gracefully.

**Wake LLM Contexts:**
If the script calls wake_llm(), the contexts will be included in the response.
This allows the LLM to receive and process wake requests from scripts.

**Return Values:**
Returns a string containing the script execution result:
• On success with return value: 'Script result: [value]' or for dict/list: 'Script result:\n[JSON formatted]'
• On success without return: 'Script executed successfully with no return value.'
• If wake_llm() called: Also includes '--- Wake LLM Contexts ---' section with context details
• On syntax error: 'Error: Syntax error in script [at line N]: [details]'
• On timeout: 'Error: Script execution timed out after [N] seconds'
• On execution error: 'Error: Script execution failed: [details]'
• On unexpected error: 'Error: Unexpected error executing script: [details]'

globals.description:
Optional dictionary of global variables to inject into the script.

These variables will be available in the script's global scope.
Useful for passing configuration, data, or context to the script.

Example:
{
  "user_email": "john@example.com",
  "project_id": 123,
  "tags": ["important", "urgent"]
}

These can then be used in the script as regular variables.

functionDeclarations.description:
Read file contents from the workspace directory. All paths are relative to the workspace root. Use this to read files from the shared workspace, task outputs, or attachments.

path.description: Relative path to the file within the workspace (e.g., 'shared/data/input.csv', 'tasks/task-123/output/report.md')

functionDeclarations.description:
Find files matching a glob pattern in the workspace. Also serves as a list/exists check for files and directories. All paths are relative to the workspace root.

functionDeclarations.name: workspace_glob

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files (e.g., '*.py', '**/*.csv', 'shared/data/*'). Use '*' to list directory contents, '**/*.ext' for recursive search.

path.description: Optional. Base directory for the search, relative to workspace root. Defaults to workspace root.

include_info.description: Optional. If true, includes file size and modification time. Useful for checking if a file exists.

max_results.description: Optional. Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 1000 to prevent performance issues with broad patterns.

functionDeclarations.description:
Delete a file or empty directory from the workspace. All paths are relative to the workspace root.

Returns: On success, returns 'OK. Deleted: [path]'. On file not found, returns 'Error: Path not found: [path]'. On non-empty directory, returns 'Error: Directory not empty: [path]'. On invalid path, returns 'Error: Invalid path: [details]'.

path.description: Relative path to the file or empty directory to delete.

titles.description: Optional. List of specific note titles to export. If not provided, exports all notes.

max_notes.description: Optional. Maximum number of notes to export. Defaults to 50.

Returns: On success, returns details of the created/updated note. On error, returns 'Error: [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: workspace_import_note

path.description: Relative path to the file within workspace (e.g., 'tasks/task-123/output/summary.md')

title.description: Optional. Title for the note. If not provided, uses the filename without extension.

include_in_prompt.description: Optional. Whether to include this note in system prompts. Takes precedence over file frontmatter; defaults to true if neither specified.

functionDeclarations.description:
Spawn an isolated AI coding agent to handle a standalone task. The worker runs in a sandboxed container with access to the shared workspace and can use Claude Code or Gemini CLI to complete coding tasks.

IMPORTANT: Workers have NO access to Family Assistant tools or data (no notes, calendar, documents, Home Assistant, etc.). They are raw coding agents only. For complex tasks that need Family Assistant context, delegate to the complex_tasks profile instead.

Use this for:
- Coding tasks requiring file manipulation in the shared workspace
- Data processing or analysis of files
- Tasks that need general-purpose computing (scripts, builds, etc.)
- Long-running operations that shouldn't block the conversation

The worker will complete the task asynchronously and notify you when done. Use read_task_result to get the output once notified.
functionDeclarations.name: spawn_worker

task_description.description: Detailed description of the task for the worker to complete. Be specific about what you want done, what files to work with, and what output is expected.

agent.description: AI coding tool to use. NOT a model checkpoint - use only the exact values listed. (default: claude)

context_paths.description: List of workspace paths to include as context for the worker (e.g., ['shared/data/input.csv', 'shared/scripts/'])

timeout_minutes.description: Maximum time for task execution in minutes (default: 30)

include_file_contents.description: Whether to include the contents of output files (default: false, just return file paths)

functionDeclarations.description:
Add a new note or update an existing note with the given title. Use this to remember information provided by the user. You can control whether the note appears in your system prompt with the include_in_prompt parameter. Notes can have attachments (images, documents) associated with them by providing attachment UUIDs.

To create a skill instead of a regular note, include YAML frontmatter with `name` and `description` fields at the top of the content (between `---` delimiters). Skills appear in the Available Skills catalog instead of the regular notes section and are loaded on demand via `get_note`.

Returns: A string indicating the operation result. On success, returns 'Note [title] has been [created/updated] successfully.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to add/update note [title]. [error details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: add_or_update_note

title.description: The unique title of the note.

include_in_prompt.description: Whether to include this note in the system prompt context. Default is true. Set to false for notes that should be searchable but not always visible.

append.description: Whether to append the content to an existing note instead of replacing it. Default is false. When true, the content will be added to the end of the existing note with a newline separator.

attachment_ids.description: Optional list of attachment UUIDs to associate with this note. These attachments will be returned when retrieving the note.

visibility_labels.description: Optional list of visibility labels for access control. Notes are only visible to profiles with matching grants. If not specified, new notes get default labels from config. Use an empty list [] to make a note visible to all profiles.

functionDeclarations.description:
Retrieve a specific note by its title to check its content, prompt inclusion status, and attachments. Returns the note's title, content, whether it's included in the system prompt, and any associated attachments.

Returns: A JSON string containing a dict with the note information. If note exists, returns {'exists': true, 'title': [title], 'content': [full content], 'include_in_prompt': [boolean], 'attachment_count': [integer]}. If note not found, returns {'exists': false, 'title': [title], 'content': null, 'include_in_prompt': null, 'attachment_count': 0}. Attachments are returned as multimodal content that vision models can see.
functionDeclarations.name: get_note

title.description: The title of the note to retrieve.

functionDeclarations.description:
List all notes with their titles, prompt inclusion status, and attachment counts. Can optionally filter to show only notes that are included or excluded from the system prompt.

Returns: A JSON string containing a list of note summaries. Returns an array where each item is {'title': [title], 'include_in_prompt': [boolean], 'content_preview': [first 100 chars], 'attachment_count': [integer]}. If no notes exist or match the filter, returns an empty array '[]'.
functionDeclarations.name: list_notes

include_in_prompt.description: Optional filter. If true, shows only notes included in prompt. If false, shows only excluded notes. If not specified, shows all notes.

functionDeclarations.description:
Delete a note by its title. This permanently removes the note from the system. Use with caution as this action cannot be undone.

Returns: A JSON string containing a dict with the operation result. On success, returns {'success': true, 'message': 'Note [title] deleted successfully.'}. If note not found, returns {'success': false, 'message': 'Note [title] not found.'}.
functionDeclarations.name: delete_note

title.description: The title of the note to delete.

functionDeclarations.description:
Delegates a specific user request to another specialized assistant profile (service) that might have different tools or capabilities. Use this if the main assistant cannot handle a request directly or if a specialized profile is more appropriate for the task. The target profile's 'delegation_security_level' (blocked, confirm, unrestricted) can override the 'confirm_delegation' parameter.

Available service profiles:
{available_service_profiles_with_descriptions}

Returns: A string containing the delegated service's response or an error message. On successful delegation, returns the text response from the target service. If service returns no text, returns 'Service [id] processed the request but provided no textual response.'. If service registry unavailable, returns 'Error: Service registry is not available to delegate the task.'. If target service not found, returns 'Error: Target service profile [id] not found.'. If delegation blocked by security policy, returns 'Error: Delegation to service profile [id] is not allowed.'. If confirmation required but unavailable, returns 'Error: Confirmation required to delegate to [id], but no confirmation mechanism is available.'. If user cancels confirmation, returns 'OK. Delegation to service [id] cancelled by user.'. If confirmation times out, returns 'Error: Confirmation timed out for delegating to [id].'. On delegation error, returns 'Error: Failed to delegate task to service [id]. Details: [error]' or 'Error from [id] service: An error occurred during processing.'.
functionDeclarations.name: delegate_to_service

target_service_id.description: The unique ID of the target service profile to delegate the request to (e.g., 'browser_profile').

user_request.description: The specific request, question, or prompt to be processed by the target service.

confirm_delegation.description: Optional. If true, explicitly ask the user for confirmation before delegating the task. Defaults to false. This may be overridden if the target profile's security level is 'confirm' (always confirm) or 'blocked' (never delegate). If the 'delegate_to_service' tool itself is configured to require confirmation for the current profile, user confirmation will also be sought.

attachment_ids.description: Optional list of attachment UUIDs to include with the delegated request. These attachments must be accessible in the current conversation and will be passed to the target service for processing.

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a reminder to be sent at a specific time. Use this tool when users ask to be reminded of something. Supports automatic follow-up reminders if the user doesn't respond.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Reminder scheduled for [time].' or 'OK. Reminder scheduled for [time] (with follow-ups every [interval], up to [N] times).' if follow-up enabled. On parameter error, returns 'Error: Invalid reminder parameters. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule the reminder.'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_reminder

reminder_time.description: The exact date and time (ISO 8601 format, including timezone, e.g., '2025-05-10T14:30:00+02:00') when the reminder should be sent.

message.description: The reminder message to send (e.g., 'Take your medication', 'Call mom', 'Submit the report').

follow_up.description: If true, will automatically send follow-up reminders if the user doesn't respond. Use for important reminders or when user says 'don't let me forget'.

follow_up_interval.description: Time between follow-up reminders (e.g., '30 minutes', '1 hour'). Only used if follow_up is true.

max_follow_ups.description: Maximum number of follow-up reminders to send. Only used if follow_up is true.

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a future trigger for yourself (the assistant) to continue processing or check on a task at a specified time. Use this for continuing work or checking task status, NOT for reminders. For reminders, use schedule_reminder instead.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Callback scheduled for [time].'. On invalid time format or past time, returns 'Error: Invalid callback time provided. Ensure it's a future ISO 8601 datetime with timezone. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule the callback.'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_future_callback

callback_time.description: The exact date and time (ISO 8601 format, including timezone, e.g., '2025-05-10T14:30:00+02:00') when the callback should be triggered.

context.description: The specific instructions or information you need to remember for the callback (e.g., 'Check if the download finished', 'Continue analyzing the data').

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a recurring LLM callback that will trigger repeatedly based on a recurrence rule (RRULE string). Use this for tasks that need to happen on a regular schedule, like daily briefings, weekly check-ins, or periodic reminders. IMPORTANT: Each recurring task creates individual callback instances that can be managed using list_pending_callbacks, modify_pending_callback, and cancel_pending_callback tools. To stop a recurring task entirely, you must cancel all its pending instances.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Recurring callback [task_id] scheduled starting [time] with rule [rule].'. On invalid arguments (RRULE format, past time), returns 'Error: Invalid arguments provided. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule the recurring task.'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_recurring_task

initial_schedule_time.description: The exact date and time (ISO 8601 format with timezone, e.g., '2025-05-15T08:00:00+00:00') when the *first* instance of the callback should run.

recurrence_rule.description: An RRULE string defining the recurrence schedule according to RFC 5545 (e.g., 'FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1;BYHOUR=8;BYMINUTE=0' for 8:00 AM daily, 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO' for every Monday).

callback_context.description: The context or instructions for the LLM when the callback triggers (e.g., 'Send a morning briefing with today's calendar events and weather', 'Check if any important emails arrived').

max_retries.description: Optional. Maximum number of retries for each instance if it fails (default: 3).

description.description: Optional. A short, URL-safe description to help identify the task (e.g., 'daily_brief', 'weekly_summary').

functionDeclarations.description:
Lists all pending LLM callback tasks for the current conversation, including:
- One-time callbacks from schedule_future_callback
- Reminder callbacks from schedule_reminder
- Individual instances of recurring tasks from schedule_recurring_task
Returns task IDs, scheduled times, and context for each pending callback.

Returns: A formatted string listing pending callbacks. If callbacks exist, returns 'Pending LLM callbacks:' followed by entries with '- Task ID: [id]
  Scheduled At: [time]
  Context: [context preview]'. If no callbacks found, returns 'No pending LLM callbacks found for this conversation.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to list pending callbacks. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: list_pending_callbacks

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of pending callbacks to list (default: 5).

functionDeclarations.description:
Modifies the scheduled time or context of a specific pending LLM callback task. You must provide the task_id of the callback to modify.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'Callback task [task_id] modified successfully.'. If neither new_callback_time nor new_context provided, returns 'Error: You must provide either a new_callback_time or a new_context to modify.'. If task not found, returns 'Error: Callback task with ID [task_id] not found.'. If task not an LLM callback, returns 'Error: Task [task_id] is not an LLM callback task.'. If task not pending, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] is not pending (current status: [status]). It cannot be modified.'. If task belongs to different conversation, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] does not belong to this conversation. Modification denied.'. On invalid new time, returns 'Error: Invalid new_callback_time. [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to modify callback task. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: modify_pending_callback

task_id.description: The unique ID of the LLM callback task to modify (obtained from list_pending_callbacks or when it was scheduled).

new_callback_time.description: Optional. The new exact date and time (ISO 8601 format, including timezone, e.g., '2025-06-01T10:00:00-07:00') for the callback. If omitted, the time is not changed.

new_context.description: Optional. The new context or instructions for the callback. If omitted, the context is not changed.

functionDeclarations.description:
Cancels a specific pending LLM callback task by its task_id. Use this to:
- Cancel one-time future callbacks
- Cancel scheduled reminders
- Cancel individual instances of recurring tasks
- Stop a recurring task by canceling all its pending instances (use list_pending_callbacks first to find them)
Note: This cancels only the specific task instance identified by task_id.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'Callback task [task_id] cancelled successfully.'. If task not found, returns 'Error: Callback task with ID [task_id] not found.'. If task not an LLM callback, returns 'Error: Task [task_id] is not an LLM callback task.'. If task not pending, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] is not pending (current status: [status]). It cannot be cancelled.'. If task belongs to different conversation, returns 'Error: Callback task [task_id] does not belong to this conversation. Cancellation denied.'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to cancel callback task. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: cancel_pending_callback

task_id.description: The unique ID of the LLM callback task to cancel (obtained from list_pending_callbacks or when it was scheduled).

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule any action (wake_llm or script) to execute at a specific time. This is the general-purpose scheduling tool that complements schedule_future_callback. Use this when you need to schedule script execution or want more control over LLM callbacks.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. [action_type] action scheduled for [schedule_time]'. If invalid action_type, returns 'Error: Invalid action_type. Must be one of: [valid types]'. If wake_llm missing context, returns 'Error: wake_llm action requires 'context' in action_config'. If script missing script_code, returns 'Error: script action requires 'script_code' in action_config'. If schedule_time in past, returns 'Error: Schedule time must be in the future'. On invalid time format, returns 'Error: Invalid schedule_time format: [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule action. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_action

schedule_time.description: When to execute the action (ISO 8601 format with timezone, e.g., '2025-05-10T14:30:00+02:00')

action_config.description: Configuration for the action. For wake_llm: {'context': 'message for LLM'}. For script: {'script_code': 'Python code', 'timeout': 600}

functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a recurring action (wake_llm or script) using RRULE format. This tool allows scheduling scripts to run on a recurring basis, complementing schedule_recurring_task which only supports LLM callbacks.

Returns: A string indicating the result. On success, returns 'OK. Recurring [action_type] action scheduled starting [start_time]' or 'OK. Recurring [action_type] action ([task_name]) scheduled starting [start_time]' if task_name provided. If invalid action_type, returns 'Error: Invalid action_type. Must be one of: [valid types]'. If wake_llm missing context, returns 'Error: wake_llm action requires 'context' in action_config'. If script missing script_code, returns 'Error: script action requires 'script_code' in action_config'. If start_time in past, returns 'Error: Start time must be in the future'. On invalid time format, returns 'Error: Invalid start_time format: [details]'. On invalid RRULE, returns 'Error: Invalid recurrence rule: [details]'. On other errors, returns 'Error: Failed to schedule recurring action. [details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: schedule_recurring_action

start_time.description: When to start the recurring schedule (ISO 8601 format with timezone)

action_config.description: Configuration for the action. For wake_llm: {'context': 'message for LLM'}. For script: {'script_code': 'Python code', 'timeout': 600}

task_name.description: Optional. A short, URL-safe description to help identify the recurring task (e.g., 'daily_weather_check', 'hourly_metrics')

functionDeclarations.description:
Search previously stored documents (emails, notes, files) using semantic and keyword matching. Returns titles and snippets of the most relevant documents.

Returns: A formatted string containing search results. On success, returns 'Found relevant documents:' followed by numbered results with Title, Source, Document ID, optional original file availability (📎), Metadata, and Snippet. When original files (PDFs, images) are available, they are indicated with 📎 symbol and file info. Use get_full_document_content to retrieve the actual file. If no results found, returns 'No relevant documents found matching the query and filters.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to execute document search. [error details]' or 'Error: Query text cannot be empty.' or 'Error: Failed to generate embedding for the query.'.
functionDeclarations.name: search_documents

query.description: The natural language query describing the information to search for.

source_types.description: Optional. Filter results to only include documents from specific sources. Common sources: 'email', 'note', 'google_drive', 'pdf', 'image'. Use ONLY if you are certain about the source type, otherwise omit this filter.

embedding_types.description: Optional. Filter results based on the type of content that was embedded. Common types: 'content_chunk', 'summary', 'title', 'ocr_text'. Use ONLY if necessary (e.g., searching only titles), otherwise omit this filter.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of results to return (default: 5).

functionDeclarations.description:
Retrieves the full content of a document in the best available format using its unique document ID (obtained from a previous search). Returns original file (PDF, image, etc.) when available, otherwise text content.

Returns: ToolResult with file attachment when original file is available, otherwise a string containing the text content. When original file exists, returns both the file as an attachment and extracted text for context. For PDFs and images, you can analyze the file directly using your multimodal capabilities. If only text content is available, returns the full text content (raw content if available, or reconstructed from chunks). If document exists but no content available, returns 'Error: Document [id] found, but no content is available.'. If document not found, returns 'Error: Document with ID [id] not found.'. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to retrieve content for document ID [id]. [error details]'. Files larger than 20MB will fallback to text-only for performance.
functionDeclarations.name: get_full_document_content

document_id.description: The unique identifier of the document whose full content is needed.

functionDeclarations.description:
Submits a document from a given URL for ingestion and indexing by the system. Use this tool if the user asks you to 'save' a web page. The document will be fetched from the URL, its content extracted, processed, and stored to be made searchable. Provide a unique source_id for tracking this ingestion request.

Returns: A string indicating the ingestion status. On success, returns 'URL submitted. Service response: [message]. Document ID: [id]. Task Enqueued: [status].'. If ingestion fails, returns 'Error submitting URL for ingestion: [message]. Details: [error details]'. If configuration missing, returns 'Error: Server configuration missing (document storage path).'. On unexpected error, returns 'Error: An unexpected error occurred while submitting the URL. [error details]'.
functionDeclarations.name: ingest_document_from_url

url_to_ingest.description: The fully qualified URL of the document to ingest.

title.description: Optional. The primary title to assign to this document. If omitted, the title will be extracted automatically during the indexing process from the web page content.

source_type.description: A category or type for this document source, e.g., 'llm_url_ingestion', 'user_link_submission'.

source_id.description: A unique identifier for this specific document within its source_type. This should be unique for each ingestion request to avoid conflicts. A UUID is a good choice if one is not readily available.

metadata_json.description: Optional. A JSON string representing a dictionary of additional key-value metadata to associate with the document (e.g., '{"category": "research", "tags": ["ai", "llm"]}').

functionDeclarations.name: get_user_documentation_content

filename.description: The exact filename of the documentation file to retrieve (e.g., 'USER_GUIDE.md'). Must end in .md or .txt.

functionDeclarations.description:
Query recent events from the event system. Returns raw event data in JSON format for examining event structure and content.

Returns: A JSON string containing event data as a dict. On success, returns {'events': [array of event objects], 'count': [number], 'hours_queried': [hours], 'source_filter': [source_id or null]}. Each event object contains: event_id, source_id, timestamp (ISO format), event_data (parsed JSON), triggered_listeners (array of IDs). If no events found, returns {'events': [], 'message': 'No events found in the last [hours] hours'}. On error, returns 'Error: Failed to query recent events. [error details]' as a string.
functionDeclarations.name: query_recent_events

hours.description: Number of hours to look back (default: 1, max: 48)
